top_choice_rationale: P001 (Crews, Deshaies, Handa) rewards a single physical principle with large generative potential: small-molecule-induced proximity of a target and an E3 ligase turns occupancy-based inhibition into event-driven, catalytic removal. Each name rests on a distinct, datable founding step (the PROTAC concept and 2001 proof of principle; identification of cereblon as the thalidomide target), the mechanism is quantitatively understood and independently reproduced over twenty-five years, and one citation about recruiting ubiquitin ligases covers both strands without a priority dispute. P003 swaps Handa for Ciulli, whose ternary-complex and VHL work deepens rather than founds the field and leaves the glue strand unrecognised, so it ranks second; P002 is mature and cleanly credited but extends the 2010 cross-coupling prize with less new principle; a prize this year is preferable to no award.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; no tie to any credited name in P001-P003. Lund colleagues Somfai and Sparr are a collegial connection only.
